summary: Focused frontend responsive regression completed on public preview URL for 390/360/320/768, including mobile menu/search/product sheet/bag flows and newsletter submission. All targeted checks passed except one reproducible 320px horizontal overflow (documentElement.scrollWidth 325 > innerWidth 320).

ui_bugs.issue: Horizontal overflow exists at 320px (scrollWidth 325 > innerWidth 320), violating no-overflow responsive requirement.
ui_bugs.selector: document.documentElement; major contributors seen in .marquee-track / horizontal rails

action_items: Fix 320px horizontal overflow so documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth across the full page.
Re-run only 320px responsive checks after fix, including modal and bag sheet overflow assertions.
Keep marquee/category rail visual behavior without increasing root scroll width.
critical_code_review_comments: 320px overflow is reproducible and should be addressed before sign-off for strict mobile-first acceptance.
Long animated/horizontal tracks should be fully clipped/contained so they do not affect root document width.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Passes: 390 mobile menu open/close, mobile search and SKU result, product bottom sheet add flow, bag open/checkout/remove/close, modal overflow checks at 390, 360 and 768, 2-column collection at 360/320, 3-column collection and split hero at 768, newsletter consent+submit success. Outstanding: only 320 page-level overflow check fails.
rca of the issue: Repro: set viewport to 320x844 on https://velaro-luxe.preview.emergentagent.com, then evaluate document.documentElement.scrollWidth vs window.innerWidth; observed 325 vs 320. Diagnostic scan shows wide moving/horizontal content (notably .marquee-track and horizontal rails) contributes to root width accounting. Mitigation: constrain overflow contributors so root width remains <= viewport (e.g., strict clipping/containment strategy on horizontal decorative tracks/rails), then retest 320.
